method.canonical: isolated tmux server; pane shell disabled echo, read one newline-terminated line, printed it between OUT markers; tmux send-keys -l supplied payload and a separate named Enter submitted it
method.raw: isolated tmux server; pane ran stty raw -echo and dd count=<payload bytes>; compared tmux send-keys -l with load-buffer from stdin plus paste-buffer; a second raw probe enabled bracketed-paste mode and verified -p -r framing

bracketed_multiline_result.wire_shape: ESC[200~ + body with literal LF bytes + ESC[201~ + CR

decision: Use a uniquely named tmux buffer loaded through stdin, paste it with -p -r so bracketed-paste and literal newline semantics are preserved, delete it as part of paste-buffer, then submit a separate named Enter.
rationale: The live probe confirms a hard 1023-byte canonical-line boundary while a raw TUI consumes 3028 bytes intact. load-buffer avoids placing the full framed body in the tmux send-keys argv; -p makes the body one bracketed paste, -r preserves framing newlines as LF, and the separate Enter preserves the no-smuggled-submit invariant. The permanent real-tmux regression now covers a 3000+ byte multiline body; the live OMP witness remains required.
